Rashi on Yoma 6a:10:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד בועל נדה כנדה אימת טבל - זה, אם בא על נדה ביום פרישתו בלילה דיוה"כ, למחר היכי עביד עבודה:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:10:1.english: For if it enters your mind [that] one who has relations with a menstruating woman is like a menstruating woman, when did he immerse? - This [applies to one] who had relations with a menstruating woman on the day of his separation, [and he immerses] on the night of Yom Kippur; [if so,] how can he perform the service the next day?

Rashi on Yoma 6a:11:1.hebrew: סמוך לשקיעת החמה - שמונה ימים לפני יוה"כ. והאי דקרי ליה שבעה, דמשום ההוא פורתא לא חשיב ליה. וטביל אור של ערב יוה"כ, ועביד למחר של ערב יוה"כ הערב שמשו:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:11:1.english: Close to sunset - Eight days before Yom Kippur. And the reason it calls it "seven" is that, because of that small amount, it does not count it [as an additional day]. And he immerses on the night [that begins] the eve of Yom Kippur, and the next day, the eve of Yom Kippur, he performs [the rite of] "the sun has set" (he-erev shemsho).

Rashi on Yoma 6a:12:1.hebrew: כל חייבי טבילות טבילתן ביום - כדיליף במסכת מגילה (דף כ.) מ"וחטאו ביום השביעי ורחץ במים" וגו' (במדבר י״ט:י״ט):
Rashi on Yoma 6a:12:1.english: All those obligated in immersions, their immersion is during the day - As it is derived in tractate Megillah (20a) from "And he shall purify him on the seventh day, and he shall wash in water" etc. (Numbers 19:19).

Rashi on Yoma 6a:12:2.hebrew: נדה ויולדת טבילתן בלילה - נדה, דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ג) שבעת ימים תהא בנדתה, כל שבעה. ויולדת, כימי נדת דוותה תטמא (שם יב):
Rashi on Yoma 6a:12:2.english: A menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth, their immersion is at night - A menstruating woman, as it is written (Leviticus 15:13): "Seven days shall she be in her impurity," all seven. And a woman after childbirth: "as in the days of the impurity of her sickness shall she be impure" (ibid. 12).

Rashi on Yoma 6a:14:1.hebrew: בעל קרי כמגע שרץ - לטבול ביום טומאתו, כדאמרינן בפרק אלו דברים בפסחים [דף סז:]. ובועל נדה כטמא מת — לטבול ביום שביעי, אלמא טובל ביום:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:14:1.english: One who had a seminal emission is like one who touched a creeping animal - [This means] to immerse on the day of his impurity, as we say in the chapter "Elu Devarim" in Pesachim [67b]. And "one who had relations with a menstruating woman is like one impure from a corpse" — [this means] to immerse on the seventh day. Thus, [it is evident that] he immerses during the day.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:14:2.hebrew: לא, לטומאתן - בעל קרי כמגע שרץ, לטומאת ערב, וראשון לטומאה. בועל נדה, טומאת שבעה, ואב הטומאה, כטמא מת:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:14:2.english: No, with regard to their impurity - One who had a seminal emission is like one who touched a creeping animal: [his impurity lasts] until evening, and he is a first-degree impurity. One who had relations with a menstruating woman has seven-day impurity, and is a primary source of impurity, like one impure from a corpse:

Rashi on Yoma 6a:15:1.hebrew: האי טומאת שבעה כתיב ביה - "ותהי נדתה עליו וטמא שבעת ימים" (שם טו):
Rashi on Yoma 6a:15:1.english: This one, impurity of seven [days] is written regarding him - "And if her menstrual impurity be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days" (Leviticus 15:24).

Rashi on Yoma 6a:1:1.hebrew: אמר לך ההוא אבנטו של כהן גדול לא זהו אבנטו וכו' - כלומר, לעולם קרא דצוואה דווקא בבת אחת, ובעשייה דפלגינהו. ללמדנו בא שאין האבנטים שוין, שנאמר במעשה האבנט של כהן גדול (שמות ל״ט:כ״ט) "ואת האבנט שש משזר תכלת וארגמן", למדנו שהוא של כלאים, דשש כיתנא ותכלת עמרא. ואבנט הבנים לא פירש הכתוב ממה היו, ואשמועינן הכא דאבנטו של כהן גדול לא זהו אבנטו של כהן הדיוט, שזה של כלאים וזה של בוץ:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:1:1.english: He could have said to you: That belt of the High Priest is not the same as his belt, etc. - That is, in truth the verse of the commandment [is] specifically [teaching that they were dressed] simultaneously, and as for the making, they were separated. [The verse] comes to teach us that the belts are not equal, for it says regarding the making of the High Priest's belt (Exodus 39:29): "And the belt of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple"; we learn that it is of mixed kinds, as shesh is linen and techelet is wool. But the belt of the sons — the verse did not specify what they were made of. And [the Gemara] teaches us here that the High Priest's belt is not the same as the belt of the common priest, since this one is of mixed kinds and that one is of fine linen.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:2:1.hebrew: זהו אבנטו - כלומר, שניהם עשויים של כלאים:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:2:1.english: This is his belt - That is to say, both of them are made of diverse kinds [of fabric, i.e., wool and linen].

Rashi on Yoma 6a:3:1.hebrew: ובבת אחת מי משכחת לה - שיהא משה לבדו חוגר חמשה בני אדם כאחת:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:3:1.english: And [can] you find [it] simultaneously? - That Moses alone would gird five people at once.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:3:2.hebrew: לא צריכא דאקדים - לא בבת אחת ממש קאמר, אלא זה אחר זה, אבל בסדר אחד היו, ולא הפסיק בגד אחר בנתיים: הלביש לאהרן כל בגדיו, ולא חגר אותו אבנט, ואח"כ הלביש את בניו מכנסים כתונת ומצנפת, ואח"כ נטל את האבנטים וחגר את אהרן, ואח"כ בניו. ולמאן דאמר אהרן ואח"כ בניו ככתבו האמור בעשייה — ויתן עליו את הכתונת ויחגור אותו באבנט וילבש אותו את המעיל, ואח"כ ויקרב את בני אהרן וילבישם כתנות ויחגור אותם באבנט — ודברי הכל לאהרן תחילה קודם שהתחיל לבניו:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:3:2.english: It is necessary only that he did so first - He does not mean literally at the same time, but rather one after the other; yet they were in one [continuous] order, and no other garment intervened in between. [Moses] dressed Aaron in all his garments, but did not gird him with the belt; and afterward he dressed his sons with the trousers, tunic, and turban; and afterward he took the belts and girded Aaron, and afterward his sons. And according to the one who says [that the order is] Aaron and afterward his sons, as it is written in the account of the making [of the garments] — "and he put the tunic upon him, and girded him with the belt, and clothed him with the robe"; and afterward "and he brought near the sons of Aaron, and clothed them with tunics, and girded them with belts" — [this is so that] according to everyone, [the belt was placed on] Aaron first, before he began with his sons.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:4:1.hebrew: אי לר' יוחנן כדאית ליה - הוא דיליף ממלואים; אי לרשב"ל כדאית ליה, הוא דיליף מסיני:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:4:1.english: Whether according to Rabbi Yochanan, as per his view - he derives it from the inauguration [days]; or whether according to Reish Lakish, as per his view, he derives it from Sinai.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:5:1.hebrew: מביתו למה פירש - מאשתו למה פירש? תבא אשתו עמו שם! שהרי על כרחך לשכת פרהדרין לא היתה קדושה, שאין ישיבה בעזרה אלא למלכי בית דוד, כ"ש שכיבה:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:5:1.english: Why did he separate from his house? - Why did he separate from his wife? Let his wife come with him there! For you must say that the Parhedrin chamber was not sanctified, since there is no sitting in the Temple courtyard except for the kings of the house of David — all the more so lying down.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:5:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: תניא, רבי יהודה בן בתירה אומר: שמא תמצא אשתו וכו':
Rashi on Yoma 6a:5:2.english: So we read: It was taught in a baraita, “Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: Lest his wife be found…” etc.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:6:1.hebrew: ברשיעי עסקינן - מה החשש? שיבא על אשתו שהיא ספק נדה:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:6:1.english: Are we dealing with wicked people? - What is the concern? That he might have relations with [his wife when she is] a possible menstruant.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:6:2.hebrew: אלא שמא יבא על אשתו ואח"כ תמצא ספק נדה - שתמצא דם על הסדין שקנחה בו, ואין ידוע אם בשעת ביאה היה בה דם זה, או לאחר ביאה. ובועל נדה טמא שבעת ימים, ויהא אסור לבוא במקדש ביום הכפורים:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:6:2.english: Rather, lest he have relations with his wife, and afterward she be found to be of uncertain menstrual status - That she finds blood on the sheet with which she wiped herself, and it is not known whether this blood was present in her at the time of intercourse or after intercourse. And one who has relations with a menstruating woman is impure for seven days, and would be forbidden to enter the Temple on Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:7:1.hebrew: כמאן כרבי עקיבא דאמר הרואה דם מטמאה את בועלה - למפרע כל מעת לעת, כשם שגזרו שמטמאה טהרות מעת לעת למפרע. ופלוגתייהו במסכת נדה בפרק כל היד (נדה דף יד.), והכי תנן: דרך בנות ישראל משמשות בשני עדים, אחד לו ואחד לה. נמצא על שלו, טמאין שניהן כל שבעה, דודאי היה דם בשעת ביאה, שאין דרך האיש לצאת ממנו דם. נמצא על שלה — אותיום, והוא לשון מיד בלשון יוני — שקנחה בפרישת יציאת השמש מיד, טמאים ודאי. נמצא לאחר זמן, כלומר שהרחיקה בדיקה, טמאים מספק. ואיזהו אחר זמן, כדי שתרד מן המטה ותדיח את פניה של מטה, ואח"כ מטמאה מעת לעת, ואינה מטמאה את בועלה. והכי פירושה: ואם יותר מכאן שהתה לבדוק ואח"כ בדקה ומצאה, הרי היא כשאר נשים, לטמא למפרע טהרות של מעת לעת, ואינה מטמאה את בועלה, שלא גזרו טומאת מעת לעת לענין טומאת בועלה. ר"ע אומר: אף מטמאה בועלה:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:7:1.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who said that a woman who sees blood renders the man who had relations with her impure - retroactively, for the entire twenty-four hours, just as they decreed that she renders pure foods impure retroactively for twenty-four hours. Their dispute is in tractate Niddah, in the chapter "Kol HaYad" (Niddah 14a). And so we learned there: The way of the daughters of Israel is to have relations using two cloths, one for him and one for her. If [blood] was found on his, both are impure for seven days, for certainly there was blood at the time of relations, since it is not the way of a man for blood to emerge from him. If it was found on hers: "Otiyom" — which is a term meaning "immediately" in the Greek language — if she wiped herself at the departure of the sun immediately, they are definitely impure. If it was found after a time — that is, she delayed the examination — they are impure out of doubt. And what is "after a time"? Enough time for her to get down from the bed and rinse her face below. And afterward, she renders [foods] impure for twenty-four hours, but she does not render the man who had relations with her impure. And this is its explanation: If she waited longer than this to examine, and afterward examined and found [blood], she is like other women: she renders pure foods retroactively impure for twenty-four hours, but she does not render the man who had relations with her impure, for they did not decree the impurity of twenty-four hours with regard to the impurity of the man who had relations with her. Rabbi Akiva says: She also renders the man who had relations with her impure:

Rashi on Yoma 6a:8:1.hebrew: אלא באחר אחר - ששהתה יותר מאחר זמן. שהזמן: אותיום ואחר זמן — לאחר אותיום, בתוך כדי שתרד ותדיח, כדקתני "איזהו אחר זמן". והתם קתני טמאים מספק, ולא פליגי עם ר"ע. ובאחר אחר זמן פליגי, כדקתני "ואח"כ מטמאה את בועלה מעת לעת". אבל בחד אחר, בתוך אחר זמן, דהיינו בתוך כדי שתרד — מודו:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:8:1.english: Only in a case of "afterward, afterward" - [i.e.,] where she waited longer than "afterward" of the [prescribed] time. For the time [is defined thus]: "Afterward" of the time is after the [examination], within the span in which she could get down [from the bed] and wash, as the Mishnah teaches: "Which is 'afterward' of the time?" And there it teaches that they are impure out of doubt, and [the Rabbis] do not disagree there with Rabbi Akiva. But in the case of "afterward" beyond the time of "afterward," they disagree, as it teaches: "And afterward, she renders her husband impure [retroactively] for a period of a day and a night." But in a case of a single "afterward," within the time of "afterward," that is, within the span in which she could get down [and wash] — they concede.

Rashi on Yoma 6a:9:1.hebrew: ש"מ - מדקתני מפרישין שבעת ימים, ואוקימנא טעמא משום חשש טומאת נדה:
Rashi on Yoma 6a:9:1.english: Learn from it - From the fact that it teaches "they sequester him for seven days," and we established that the reason is due to the concern for the impurity of a menstruating woman.

Tosafot on Yoma 6a:1:1.hebrew: אמר לך אבנטו של כהן גדול לא זהו אבנטו כו' - וא"ת: היכי דייק מדכתיב אותו, הכתיב נמי אותם, ומאותם נימא שהאבנטי' שוין? וא"כ, קרא לא כמר דייקי ולא כמר דייקי. וי"ל: סברא הוא לאוקמא קרא דואת האבנט תעשה שש משזר וגו' בכהן גדול דווקא, כיון דשאר בגדיו היו נמי דכלאים — אפוד (ומעיל); אבל הדיוט, דכל שאר בגדיו דבוץ, נימא נמי אבנטו דבוץ. ואשכחן נמי כי האי גוונא: כהן גדול ביום הכפורים, לפי שהיו שאר בגדיו דבוץ, היה נמי אבנטו דבוץ. וה"ר מנחם מיואני זצ"ל פירש דנפקא ליה מג"ש דרוקם רוקם, דכתיב בואתה תצוה: ואת האבנט תעשה מעשה רוקם, ובכהן גדול מיירי, מדכתיב: ולבני אהרן תעשה כתנות ועשית להם אבנטים ומגבעות; ואם כן, קמא דכהן גדול. ובפרשת פקודי כתיב בשעת עשייה: ואת האבנט שש משזר תכלת וארגמן ותולעת שני מעשה רוקם, וילפינן בגזירה שוה דכמו דאותו רוקם כלאים הוה, כך ואבנט תעשה מעשה רוקם שכתב בכ"ג כלאים הוה. אבל באבנט של כהן הדיוט לא כתב רוקם. ולמאן דאמר דתרוייהו של כלאים, משוה להן מדכתיב אותם:
Tosafot on Yoma 6a:1:1.english: "He could have said to you: The belt of the High Priest is not this belt [of the common priest]" etc. - And if you say: How does [the Gemara] infer [that they were dressed separately] from the fact that it is written "him" (otו)? It is also written "them" (otam), and from "them" let us say that the belts are the same! And if so, the verse supports neither this Sage's inference nor that Sage's inference. And one can answer: It is reasoning to establish the verse "And you shall make the belt of fine twined linen..." etc. as referring specifically to the High Priest, since his other garments were also of diverse kinds (kilayim) — the ephod (and the robe); but for the common priest, whose other garments are all of linen, let us say that his belt too is of linen. And we also find something like this: the High Priest on Yom Kippur, because his other garments were of linen, his belt too was of linen. And Rabbi Menachem of Joigny, of blessed memory, explained that [the Gemara] derives it from the verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) of "embroidery" (rokem) — "embroidery": as it is written in [the portion] "You shall command": "And the belt you shall make of embroidered work," and it is speaking of the High Priest, since it is written: "And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics, and you shall make for them belts and caps"; and if so, the first [verse] is about the High Priest. And in the portion Pekudei it is written at the time of the making: "And the belt of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet, of embroidered work," and we learn by gezerah shavah that just as the "embroidery" of the [ephod, mentioned there], is of diverse kinds, so too the belt that is "made of embroidered work," which [the Torah] wrote regarding the High Priest, is of diverse kinds. But regarding the belt of the common priest, it did not write "embroidery." And according to the one who says that both are of diverse kinds, he equates them from the fact that it is written "them."

Tosafot on Yoma 6a:5:1.hebrew: מביתו למה פירש - פי' רש"י: תבא אשתו עמו שם, שהרי על כרחך לשכת פרהדרין לא היתה קדושה, שאין ישיבה בעזרה, כ"ש שכיבה. וקשיא לן: דנהי דלא קדישא כקדושת עזרה, מ"מ כהר הבית היתה, דאמרי' בפרק פרת חטאת (זבחים דף קטו:) דכל הר הבית מחנה לויה הוא, ובעל קרי אינו רשאי ליכנס במחנה לויה, דאמר בפסחים פרק אלו דברים (פסחים דף סז:): זב — וכל זב, לרבות בעל קרי. אלא יש לפרש: מביתו למה פירש — הוה לן למימר שיפרישוהו למחילה אחת בהר הבית, דאמרי' פרק כיצד צולין (פסחים דף פו.) דמחילות לא נתקדשו:
Tosafot on Yoma 6a:5:1.english: "Why did he separate from his house?" - Rashi explained: His wife should come with him there, since you must say that the Parhedrin Chamber was not sanctified, as sitting is not permitted in the Temple courtyard, all the more so lying down. But this is difficult for us: Granted that it was not sanctified with the sanctity of the courtyard, nevertheless it was like the Temple Mount, for we say in the chapter "Parat Chatat" (Zevachim 115b) that the entire Temple Mount is the camp of the Levites, and a ba'al keri (one who had a seminal emission) may not enter the camp of the Levites, as it says in Pesachim, chapter "Eilu Devarim" (Pesachim 67b): "a zav" — "any zav," to include a ba'al keri. Rather, one should explain: "Why did he separate from his house?" — we should have said that they should separate him to one chamber on the Temple Mount, for we say in the chapter "Keitzad Tzolin" (Pesachim 86a) that the chambers were not sanctified:
